paragraphs: Motor decoding connects recorded brain activity to movement-related behavior. Much previous work has made this problem manageable by restricting the complexity of the recordings or behaviors being studied. This paper investigates a different approach: combining a broad collection of neural recordings to train one model that can support multiple downstream decoding tasks.

The researchers pretrain an autoregressive Transformer using 2,000 hours of neural population spiking activity recorded through intracortical microelectrodes. These recordings are paired with diverse movement-related measurements and come from more than 30 monkeys and humans. The breadth of this training collection lets the study examine whether a shared model can provide useful decoding capabilities across varied settings.

The resulting model benefits eight downstream decoding tasks and generalizes across several shifts in neural data distributions. These findings support broad pretraining as a useful direction for motor decoding. The authors also identify a boundary: simply scaling autoregressive Transformers appears unlikely to overcome variability between sensors or the limited variety of outputs represented in neural datasets.
neurips-2025-a-generalist-intracortical-.tldr: A Transformer pretrained on diverse intracortical recordings improves motor decoding across tasks, while sensor variability and stereotyped outputs remain obstacles to scaling.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary learning must handle categories absent from its observed training examples. Estimating the distribution of this broader environment using only familiar categories leaves a fundamental gap: the missing categories prevent the estimation error from being identified. This paper investigates whether generating examples of unseen categories can make that error more tractable.

The authors provide a theoretical argument that generating unseen-class data can enable distribution estimation with an upper bound on its error. Their method turns this insight into a data generation pipeline organized around both categories and domains. A hierarchical semantic tree guides which categories to generate, while information inferred from the observed data guides the domain characteristics of those examples.

A distribution alignment algorithm then uses the generated examples to estimate and maximize posterior probabilities, with the aim of improving generalization beyond observed categories. Experiments across 11 datasets report improvements over baseline approaches of up to 14%. This maximum reported gain supports the method's effectiveness in the evaluated settings; the theoretical contribution concerns bounding estimation error through inclusion of generated unseen-class data.
neurips-2025-beyond-the-seen-bounded-dis.tldr: Generating unseen-category examples enables bounded distribution estimation and improves open-vocabulary learning in experiments across 11 datasets.

paragraphs: Reducing the rank of selected language-model weight matrices can improve downstream accuracy without conventional fine-tuning. The practical obstacle is finding which matrices to modify: the earlier LASER approach requires an expensive search with repeated evaluations over a full dataset. This paper develops a faster way to identify promising compression changes.

The method uses gradients of matrix singular values to identify a small set of candidates, avoiding an exhaustive sweep through the layers. It also expands the available factorizations by clustering matrix rows around multiple subspaces and decomposing each cluster separately. The authors report that this added flexibility reduces overfitting to the original training data and raises accuracy by up to 24.6 percentage points.

In the studied settings, 100 examples suffice for computing the indicative gradients and evaluating candidate accuracy. The authors attribute this finding to adaptation being driven mainly by prompting style rather than dataset size. Combining a single gradient step with a short search over candidate layers and factorizations produces their adaptation algorithm. The gradient serves the selection process, while adaptation is achieved through matrix reduction without fine-tuning.
neurips-2025-compress-to-impress-efficie.tldr: A single gradient step on 100 examples guides selective matrix compression that adapts language models without conventional fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Visual storytelling requires a subject to remain recognizable across several generated images. A text-to-image model may produce convincing individual pictures while changing the subject's appearance from one scene to the next. This paper addresses that cross-image consistency problem through the generation procedure, without training the model on a story visualization dataset.

The proposed strategy combines zigzag sampling, asymmetric prompts, and visual sharing. The sampling mechanism alternates asymmetric prompting to help retain subject characteristics. Alongside this, a visual sharing module carries visual cues between generated images. These components address consistency through both the textual guidance used during sampling and information transferred across the images in the story.

Quantitative measurements and qualitative evaluations show that the method significantly outperforms previous approaches in the reported experiments. Its contribution is a training-free way to make a sequence of generated pictures more coherent, especially in how subjects are depicted. This matters because story quality depends on relationships between images as well as the quality of each image considered separately.
neurips-2025-consistent-story-generation.tldr: A training-free sampling strategy combines asymmetric prompts and shared visual cues to improve subject consistency across generated story images.

paragraphs: Long reasoning traces can contain unnecessary steps that consume computation and sometimes hurt answer quality. This paper hypothesizes that part of the problem comes from choosing unsuitable reasoning strategies at particular moments. It treats reasoning as a sequence of modular thinking patterns whose usefulness can be assessed and improved.

The authors segment generated reasoning paths into these patterns, promote helpful ones, and remove detrimental ones. In their analysis, the resulting paths reduce attention computation by up to 47% while preserving accuracy for responses that were originally correct. Some initially incorrect responses also become correct, with a reported 15.6% accuracy improvement alongside shorter reasoning. These results concern the optimized paths themselves.

The authors then use pairs of suboptimal and optimized paths for preference optimization, teaching models to favor the improved reasoning behavior. Evaluations on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks report accuracy gains of up to 12% and a reduction from approximately 5,000 to 3,000 tokens. The findings suggest that selecting and arranging useful reasoning patterns can improve both efficiency and accuracy in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-dont-think-longer-think-wis.tldr: Optimizing the choice and placement of reasoning patterns produces shorter reasoning paths and improves mathematical reasoning accuracy in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Training large speech-recognition Transformers through federated learning is difficult because gradients can behave very differently across layers. Standard optimization may struggle to converge even before differential privacy is added. This paper establishes a benchmark and training recipe for combining federated learning with user-level differential privacy in end-to-end speech recognition.

The approach clips gradients separately for each layer and applies layer-wise gradient normalization. The theoretical analysis finds that these two techniques jointly reduce clipping bias and differences in gradient behavior across layers. Their combination addresses optimization problems that become especially important in deeper models, rather than treating every layer's updates as though they had similar scales.

The empirical viability claim depends on populations of at least several million users. When extrapolating to higher and lower population scales, the authors report user-level privacy parameters of (7.2, 10⁻⁹) and (4.5, 10⁻⁹), alongside absolute word-error-rate performance penalties of 1.3% and 4.6%, respectively. The findings support a practical route to private federated speech recognition at those scales and offer broader guidance about managing layer-wise gradient heterogeneity in large models.
neurips-2025-enabling-differentially-pri.tldr: Layer-wise clipping and normalization enable promising private federated speech recognition results when extrapolated to populations of several million users.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to adapt large pretrained models of physical systems while training only a limited number of parameters. Its focus is Large Operator Models built from scaled variants of the Fourier Neural Operator. The authors find that LoRA, a widely used adaptation method, performs markedly worse than adapter tuning for these models.

Their theoretical analysis connects this difference to approximation within Fourier layers. Stacked LoRA has an approximation-error lower bound that grows with depth, whereas adapters retain universal approximation capacity. By concentrating parameters on low-frequency modes carrying most of the energy, adapters achieve exponentially decreasing error with bottleneck width in the analyzed Fourier-domain setting. The paper also characterizes the relevant physical solutions as spectrally sparse.

These findings motivate F-Adapter, which assigns larger adapter modules to low-frequency components and smaller modules to high-frequency components. This makes the allocation of trainable capacity depend on spectral structure. Across multiple challenging three-dimensional Navier–Stokes benchmarks, the method reports state-of-the-art results, improving generalization and fidelity to frequency content over LoRA and other parameter-efficient adaptation techniques.
neurips-2025-f-adapter-frequency-adaptiv.tldr: F-Adapter allocates adaptation capacity by frequency, improving physical-system modeling over LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods on 3D Navier–Stokes benchmarks.

paragraphs: The m-set semi-bandit problem requires a learner to select exactly m options from d possibilities at every round. The goal is to limit regret, the accumulated disadvantage relative to the comparison strategy. A known optimal adversarial regret bound is achieved by Follow-the-Regularized-Leader, but that policy must repeatedly solve optimization problems to obtain selection probabilities.

This paper analyzes Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader as a simpler selection procedure. It adds random perturbations to estimated losses and chooses the m options with the smallest resulting values. With Fréchet perturbations, the authors prove an adversarial regret bound of order √(nm)(√(d log d) + m^(5/6)), where n is the number of rounds. This approaches the known optimal order of √(nmd).

The same approach achieves logarithmic regret in the stochastic setting, bringing it close to desirable guarantees in both environments. The paper also proves lower bounds showing that the additional factors cannot be removed within the authors' approach. Its contribution therefore combines a simpler decision rule with strong guarantees while identifying a specific theoretical barrier to further improvement.
neurips-2025-follow-the-perturbed-leader.tldr: Fréchet-perturbed leader selection achieves near-optimal adversarial regret and logarithmic stochastic regret for m-set semi-bandits, with approach-specific lower bounds.

paragraphs: A detailed causal graph can be impractical to specify when a system contains many variables. Cluster-directed mixed graphs provide a higher-level description by grouping variables together. This paper asks whether causal effects between such groups can be identified when the underlying system also permits cyclic causal relationships.

The setting uses input-output structural causal models, which allow cycles and induce directed mixed graphs. The authors prove that do-calculus is sound and complete for identifying macro causal effects in cluster graphs over these graphs. Soundness means its identification steps are valid; completeness means it can identify effects whenever identification is possible within the stated framework. Unlike the cited result for underlying acyclic graphs, this theorem does not require every cluster to contain more than one variable.

The paper also extends earlier graphical criteria for showing that a macro causal effect cannot be identified. That extension applies to a subset of the cyclic setting. Together, the results strengthen the theoretical basis for causal reasoning with grouped variables and structural feedback, without implying that every effect in such a system is identifiable.
neurips-2025-identifying-macro-causal-ef.tldr: The paper proves soundness and completeness of do-calculus for macro causal effects in cluster graphs over cyclic directed mixed graphs, without a cluster-size restriction.

paragraphs: Vision-language models that encode images as discrete tokens can describe objects that are absent from an image. This paper investigates a possible explanation: training may associate tokens that frequently appear together with the same object descriptions. Present tokens could then evoke associated but visually absent tokens, contributing to hallucinated objects.

To investigate this hypothesis, the authors build an image-token co-occurrence graph from a segmentation dataset. They use a graph neural network with contrastive learning, followed by clustering, to group tokens found in similar visual contexts. Hallucinations predominantly correspond to clusters whose tokens dominate the input. Within those clusters, absent tokens correlate much more strongly with hallucinated objects than tokens actually present in the image.

The proposed intervention modifies latent image embeddings during generation to suppress the influence of these visually absent tokens. Experiments report reduced hallucination while preserving expressivity. The findings connect a measured pattern of token associations to a targeted mitigation method; the proposed explanation begins as a hypothesis, supported by the reported correlations and intervention results.
neurips-2025-image-token-matters-mitigat.tldr: Editing latent image embeddings to suppress associated but absent image tokens reduces hallucinations while preserving expressivity in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Some data occupy a curved, lower-dimensional structure inside a larger space. This paper studies how ordinary Euclidean diffusion models can sample such manifold-structured data directly. The authors identify a source of inaccurate generation: the score function used by diffusion develops singular behavior at multiple scales in the surrounding space.

Their theoretical analysis separates the score into directions tangent to the manifold and directions normal to it. Tangential directions follow the data's underlying structure, while normal directions point away from it. This decomposition exposes the structure of the singularity and motivates two methods aimed at improving the accuracy of generated samples.

Niso-DM uses non-isotropic noise, allowing different directions to receive different noise scales, to reduce scale discrepancies in the score function. Tango-DM instead trains only its tangential component through a corresponding loss. Numerical experiments report superior performance on distributions supported by manifolds with varied, complex geometries. The work connects a geometric analysis of sampling error to two concrete changes in diffusion modeling.
neurips-2025-improving-the-euclidean-dif.tldr: Two diffusion methods improve sampling of manifold data by addressing score-function singularities through directional noise or tangential-only training.

paragraphs: An image-processing network can make individually plausible predictions that flicker when applied frame by frame to video. Changing corruption across frames can make this instability worse. This paper introduces adapters intended to make existing frame-based networks produce more stable video predictions while also handling corrupted inputs more robustly.

The stability adapters can be inserted into a broad range of architectures and trained through a resource-efficient procedure that keeps the base network frozen. The authors introduce a combined accuracy, stability, and robustness loss to describe these objectives within one framework. They analyze the loss theoretically and identify conditions under which it leads to well-behaved stabilizer training.

Experiments cover denoising with NAFNet, enhancement with HDRNet, monocular depth with Depth Anything v2, and semantic segmentation with DeepLabv3+. Across these tasks, the method improves temporal stability and robustness to corruptions including compression artifacts, noise, and adverse weather, while maintaining or improving prediction quality. The results support adapters as a broadly applicable way to extend image models to more consistent video inference.
neurips-2025-instant-video-models-univer.tldr: Trainable stability adapters improve the consistency and corruption robustness of frame-based networks on video while keeping the base model frozen.

paragraphs: Recognizing objects in remote-sensing images becomes harder when instructions describe them indirectly or require interpretation beyond an explicit category name. This paper introduces instruction-oriented counting, detection, and segmentation tasks, together with EarthInstruct. The benchmark combines two remote-sensing datasets with different resolutions and annotation rules across 20 categories, requiring models to interpret dataset-specific instructions.

The proposed InstructSAM framework requires no additional training. A large vision-language model interprets the instruction and estimates object counts, while SAM2 proposes segmentation masks. The system then assigns labels to masks through binary integer programming. Combining semantic similarity with count constraints lets it make these assignments without confidence thresholds.

Experiments show that InstructSAM matches or exceeds specialized baselines across multiple tasks. Its inference time remains nearly constant as object count changes in the reported evaluations. Compared with direct generation approaches, it reduces output tokens by 89% and total runtime by more than 32%. The framework demonstrates how instruction interpretation, mask proposals, and constrained assignment can jointly support efficient remote-sensing recognition.
neurips-2025-instructsam-a-training-free.tldr: InstructSAM combines instruction interpretation, segmentation masks, and count-constrained label assignment for efficient, training-free remote-sensing object recognition.

paragraphs: Post-training quantization reduces language-model storage requirements by representing weights with fewer bits. At very low bit widths, ordinary uniform quantization can noticeably reduce model accuracy. This paper proposes Grouped Lattice Vector Quantization, which gives different groups of weights their own learned structure for representing compressed values.

Each weight group receives a customized lattice codebook defined by a learnable generation matrix. Training such a system is difficult because quantization is not differentiable. The authors use Babai rounding to approximate the search for the nearest lattice point during training, enabling stable optimization of the matrices that define the codebooks. This makes the representation adaptable to each group of weights.

After training, decoding the compressed representation requires a matrix-vector multiplication, keeping that stage simple. Experiments on multiple benchmarks report a better balance between model size and accuracy than existing post-training quantization baselines. The contribution is therefore both a learned, group-specific quantization framework and a practical decoding procedure aimed at deploying large models under tight resource constraints.
neurips-2025-learning-grouped-lattice-ve.tldr: Learned lattice codebooks customized to weight groups improve the model-size–accuracy trade-off of low-bit language-model quantization.

paragraphs: Preference optimization can help multimodal language models reduce hallucination by learning which responses should be favored. Existing approaches use visual contrastive objectives to increase attention to image inputs. This paper identifies two weaknesses in those approaches: insufficiently rigorous optimization objectives and preference supervision that reaches the model indirectly.

The proposed Symmetric Multimodal Preference Optimization method uses response pairs to provide direct preference supervision for improving visual understanding. It organizes learning symmetrically while preserving theoretical consistency with standard Direct Preference Optimization. This alignment is central to the contribution: the method changes how multimodal preferences are used while retaining a rigorous connection to the underlying preference-optimization framework.

SymMPO also introduces a preference margin consistency loss. Ordinary ordinal preference learning indicates which response should rank higher; the added loss regulates the size of the preference gap between symmetric pairs. Evaluations across five benchmarks report superior performance and support the method's effectiveness in reducing multimodal hallucination. The findings suggest that both direct supervision and control over preference margins can contribute to better visual grounding.
neurips-2025-mitigating-hallucination-th.tldr: SymMPO combines theoretically aligned symmetric preference learning with preference-gap consistency to reduce multimodal hallucination across five benchmarks.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input differs from the data a model is expected to handle. Many methods use only the final representation produced by a large pretrained model. This paper examines information available earlier in the network and finds that intermediate layers can provide rich, varied signals of distributional change.

The authors connect these signals to representations shaped by residual connections, which progressively transform input projections. To exploit differences between layers, they introduce an entropy-based criterion that automatically selects layers carrying complementary information. The selection procedure requires neither additional training nor access to out-of-distribution examples, making the existing model's internal representations the central resource.

Selectively incorporating intermediate representations improves reported detection accuracy by up to 10% on far-out-of-distribution benchmarks and by more than 7% on near-out-of-distribution benchmarks relative to state-of-the-art training-free methods. The evaluations span several architectures and training objectives. These findings show that useful detection information can be distributed across model depth and that the value of those signals is influenced by how the model is built and trained.
neurips-2025-mysteries-of-the-deep-role-.tldr: An entropy-based, training-free selection of intermediate model layers improves out-of-distribution detection without requiring out-of-distribution examples.

paragraphs: Zeroth-order optimization adapts a model using information from objective evaluations rather than directly computing ordinary gradients. This paper develops PaZO, a preconditioned and accelerated method for fine-tuning language models in that setting. Its central concern is how to improve convergence by changing the way estimated optimization directions are scaled.

The authors first show theoretically that zeroth-order stochastic gradient descent alone does not achieve the ideal convergence rate considered in their analysis. They introduce Preconditioned Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation and a theoretical version of PaZO. Setting the preconditioner's order to −1/2 in the proposed formulation yields an improved convergence rate, connecting the choice of scaling to the algorithm's theoretical behavior.

A practical version uses a diagonal estimate of the Hessian together with a moving average to stabilize training. Experiments cover diverse downstream tasks and models including RoBERTa-large and OPT. PaZO performs better than the other zeroth-order baselines in the reported comparisons. The contribution links a theoretical case for preconditioning to a usable optimization method for language-model adaptation.
neurips-2025-pazo-preconditioned-acceler.tldr: PaZO uses theoretically motivated preconditioning and practical stabilization to improve zeroth-order language-model fine-tuning over evaluated baselines.

paragraphs: A language model analyzing a table needs to recognize problems in the data as well as answer the question. Missing values, outliers, and logical inconsistencies can change which conclusions are justified. RADAR evaluates this form of data awareness: whether models notice, reason about, and appropriately handle artifacts in tabular data.

The benchmark uses programmatic perturbations to introduce artifacts in a controlled way. It contains 2,980 table-query pairs grounded in real-world data from nine domains and covers five artifact types. Table size is also varied systematically, allowing the evaluation to examine how reasoning behaves as the amount of tabular information increases.

The reported evaluations find a substantial drop in frontier-model performance when artifacts are introduced, despite decent results on tables without them. This exposes a gap between answering questions over clean data and handling imperfect data responsibly within the analysis. RADAR's support for different perturbations and adjustable table sizes provides a flexible way to investigate that gap and evaluate progress in data-aware reasoning.
neurips-2025-radar-benchmarking-language.tldr: RADAR reveals substantial weaknesses in language models' handling of imperfect tables through controlled tests of data artifacts and table size.

paragraphs: Continually updating a multimodal language model requires finding the relevant knowledge and applying it to the right inputs. CARML addresses both parts through retrieval-augmented editing. The paper focuses on unreliable matching in large knowledge collections and insufficient coordination between the different forms of guidance used during editing.

Its retrieval mechanism measures uncertainty within modalities and conflict between modalities, then uses these measurements to combine retrieval results dynamically. An edit-scope classifier checks whether an incoming example falls within the scope of the retrieved knowledge. For examples judged in scope, the framework converts that knowledge into continuous prompt prefixes that guide the model implicitly.

These prefixes combine a static component capturing textual meaning with a dynamic, token-level component representing context-sensitive cross-modal associations. CARML also applies an explicit correction mechanism that uses label knowledge to adjust output logits. Experiments across multiple multimodal models and datasets report superior performance in lifelong editing scenarios. The method brings together relevance assessment, scope checking, implicit prompts, and explicit output correction to improve the reliability of ongoing knowledge updates.
neurips-2025-reliable-lifelong-multimoda.tldr: CARML combines conflict-aware retrieval, edit-scope checks, continuous prompts, and explicit output correction to improve lifelong multimodal knowledge editing.

paragraphs: Vertex hunting estimates the corners of a simplex from noisy points. A simplex represents combinations of its vertices, so recovering those vertices can reveal structure in data expressed as mixtures. This paper introduces a semi-supervised version in which some points come with partial information about their position within that mixture geometry.

The available information takes the form of barycentric coordinates, which describe a point through its contributions from the simplex's vertices. However, these coordinates are known only through an unknown transformation. The authors develop a method based on properties of orthogonal projection matrices, using linear-algebraic insights to make this incomplete information useful for estimating the simplex.

The paper establishes theoretical error bounds and shows a faster convergence rate than existing unsupervised vertex-hunting algorithms. It then applies the method to estimating mixed community memberships in networks and to semi-supervised topic modeling, producing efficient and scalable algorithms. The contribution shows how partial structural information can improve geometric estimation even when that information is not directly available in its original coordinate form.
neurips-2025-semi-supervised-vertex-hunt.tldr: Semi-supervised vertex hunting uses transformed partial coordinate information to recover simplex structure with faster theoretical convergence than unsupervised alternatives.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a scene's three-dimensional structure and understanding its contents are closely related tasks. Recent systems connect them by aligning two-dimensional and three-dimensional features, which can limit understanding and lose semantic information. SIU3R introduces a framework that performs both tasks from images without supplied camera poses, without requiring alignment to a separate two-dimensional model.

The framework connects reconstruction and understanding through a pixel-aligned 3D representation. It also expresses multiple understanding tasks through a shared set of learnable queries, allowing understanding to operate directly within the 3D framework. The authors analyze how the two tasks benefit one another and introduce two lightweight modules to facilitate interaction through their shared representation.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on reconstruction, understanding, and their simultaneous execution. These findings support both the shared representation and the modules designed to encourage cooperation between tasks. Here, alignment-free refers to removing the requirement for alignment with 2D models; the architecture still deliberately links pixels to its 3D representation so that geometry and meaning can be handled together.
neurips-2025-siu3r-simultaneous-scene-un.tldr: SIU3R jointly reconstructs and understands 3D scenes from unposed images through a shared representation without alignment to 2D models.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can improve vision-language reasoning while encouraging models to produce lengthy reasoning traces for every answer. This paper studies whether a model can learn when such a trace is useful. The aim is selective reasoning: spending output tokens on thought when needed and bypassing unnecessary reasoning on easier questions.

The training strategy has two stages. During supervised fine-tuning, thought dropout randomly replaces reasoning traces with empty thoughts, introducing a format that permits either reasoning or a direct answer. Group Relative Policy Optimization then allows the model to explore both choices while optimizing task-aware outcome rewards. The first stage provides a starting behavior; the second learns how to use it.

Experiments report completion-length reductions of up to 90% relative to vanilla GRPO, with performance maintained or sometimes improved. Evaluations span language, vision-language, and agentic tasks using models with three billion and seven billion parameters. Across these settings, the models increasingly bypass unnecessary reasoning as training progresses, supporting learned control over when to generate explicit thought.
neurips-2025-think-or-not-selective-reas.tldr: Thought dropout followed by reinforcement learning teaches selective reasoning, reducing completion length by up to 90% without sacrificing reported task performance.

paragraphs: Visual in-context learning adapts a model to a task through examples included in its context. Choosing these examples can be treated as ranking a pool of candidates. This paper questions the common assumption that greater visual similarity to a query reliably identifies better examples, noting that this assumption lacks sufficient justification.

The authors also examine how Partial2Global builds an overall ranking from sampled pairwise preferences. Random sampling can leave some comparisons poorly covered while repeatedly selecting others. Their enhanced method, RH-Partial2Global, uses jackknife conformal prediction to construct reliable alternative sets and a covering-design sampling strategy to obtain comprehensive, uniform coverage of pairwise preferences.

The approach therefore addresses both the reliability of the candidate alternatives and the structure of the comparisons used to rank them. Experiments across diverse visual tasks show that RH-Partial2Global outperforms Partial2Global. The findings support more systematic prompt selection, where the quality of a global ranking depends on how candidates and comparisons are assembled as well as on the individual preference predictions.
neurips-2025-towards-reliable-and-holist.tldr: RH-Partial2Global improves visual in-context example selection using conformal prediction and systematically balanced pairwise comparisons.

paragraphs: N:M pruning keeps N weights in each consecutive group of M, creating patterns that hardware can accelerate. Ordinary patterns may disappear when a weight matrix is transposed, limiting their usefulness during training. TSENOR addresses the construction of masks that satisfy the sparsity structure in both orientations and scale to billion-parameter models.

The method formulates mask generation as optimal transport problems. It solves them using entropy regularization and Dykstra's algorithm, then applies rounding to obtain masks. A tensor-based implementation uses GPU parallelism, reporting speedups of up to 100 times with 1–10% error relative to existing methods. The approach supports arbitrary N:M values and integrates with pruning frameworks including Wanda, SparseGPT, and ALPS.

In experiments, a transposable 16:32 sparse LLaMA3.2-8B model performs close to its standard N:M counterpart and better than a standard 2:4 sparse model. These results show the practical value of making a wider range of transposable patterns computationally accessible. The reported speedup concerns finding masks, while transposability addresses the structural requirement for acceleration across matrix orientations.
neurips-2025-tsenor-highly-efficient-alg.tldr: TSENOR efficiently constructs transposable N:M pruning masks at billion-parameter scale, enabling flexible sparsity patterns with promising model-quality results.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning draws a sample's representation toward its augmented version while separating it from other samples. This paper investigates why that objective can produce useful representations by analyzing dimensionality reduction in Gaussian mixture models. The setting provides a structured way to study what information contrastive learning can recover without mixture-component labels.

Because an ordinary Gaussian mixture model does not define augmentations, the authors introduce coupled sample pairs. The augmentation is noisy but biased toward the component that generated the original sample. In this setting, they show that InfoNCE can recover the optimal lower-dimensional subspace even when Gaussian components are non-isotropic. It can match supervised linear discriminant analysis despite the noisy augmentations.

The paper also extends its modeling setup to multiple modalities to study the CLIP contrastive loss. Experiments on CIFAR100 provide supporting empirical evidence: representations learned with InfoNCE match linear discriminant analysis on clustering metrics. The theoretical conclusion is tied to the proposed mixture and augmentation setting, while the real-data result shows a corresponding comparison in the reported experiment.
neurips-2025-understanding-contrastive-l.tldr: In a Gaussian-mixture setting with noisy coupled augmentations, InfoNCE can recover an optimal subspace and match supervised linear discriminant analysis.
